GoPro will lay off about 23% of its workforce, or roughly 145 employees, by the end of 2026 as part of a restructuring plan aimed at reducing costs and improving profitability. The company said the layoffs will begin in the second quarter and are expected to cost between $11.5 million and $15 million, primarily due to severance and healthcare obligations. The move follows a $9 million quarterly loss reported in 2025 and reflects increasing pressure on hardware makers operating in a crowded and slowing market.
